**5B.4 Research Note**

**Bottom line**
Tinubu’s 2024 record is mixed, leaning positive on formal pro-business rule-setting and investment climate, but weakened by severe macro stress, some opacity, and a coercive policy environment that could chill entrepreneurship and competition.

**Accepted claims**

- **President Tinubu Establishes Comprehensive Economic Coordination and Planning System for Nigeria** | State House | 2024-03-27 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/) | Tinubu created PECC and EET structures centered on the finance minister and CBN governor, with economists and private-sector figures, which is strong evidence of a rule-setting, technocratic approach to investment and job creation. | `5B.4`, `5B.2`, `5B.3`
- **President Tinubu directs reorganisation of the Bureau of Public Procurement** | State House | 2024-06-15 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/) | Direct procurement reform and transparency push suggests an attempt to make state purchasing rules more predictable and less rent-seeking, which matters for fair competition and property-right-like security in contracting. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`
- **President Tinubu appoints new Director-General of the Bureau of Public Enterprises** | State House | 2024-06-15 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-new-director-general-of-the-bureau-of-public-enterprises/) | The appointee was presented as a financial expert and chartered accountant, signaling technocratic stewardship of enterprise reform and privatization-related governance. | `5B.4`, `5B.2`, `5B.3`
- **President Tinubu appoints management team of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund** | State House | 2024-04-05 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-management-team-of-the-nigerian-education-loan-fund/) | Tinubu framed the team as qualified professionals tasked with building a long-horizon social investment institution, which supports job creation and human-capital formation. | `5B.4`, `5B.2`, `5B.3`
- **President Tinubu appoints new board of Family Homes Fund** | State House | 2024-07-02 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-new-board-of-family-homes-fund/) | The presidency explicitly described the board as qualified Nigerians expected to use expertise to grow the real-estate sector, a positive signal for investment and housing-market rules. | `5B.4`, `5B.2`
- **Nigeria: 2024 Article IV Consultation - Press Release, Staff Report, Staff Statement, and Statement by the Executive Director for Nigeria** | IMF | 2024-05-09 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/05/08/nigeria-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-staff-statement-and-548726) | IMF welcomed subsidy removal, FX unification, and revenue/governance measures, which are core rule changes for investment and market fairness even though they imposed major adjustment costs. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`
- **Turning the Corner: Nigeria’s Ongoing Path of Economic Reforms** | World Bank | 2024-06-13 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/06/13/turning-the-corner-nigeria-ongoing-path-of-economic-reforms) | The World Bank said reforms reduced distortions and improved transparency, especially by narrowing the official/parallel FX gap and phasing out the regressive fuel subsidy. That supports fairer market rules and better investment conditions. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`
- **Supporting Nigeria’s Homegrown Reforms: New World Bank Financing for Inclusive Growth and Revenue Diversification** | World Bank | 2024-06-13 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/13/supporting-nigeria-homegrown-reforms-new-world-bank-financing-for-inclusive-growth-and-revenue-diversification) | The Bank said the package aimed to raise non-oil revenue, safeguard oil revenue, and create fiscal space for public services while supporting 15 million households, which is strong evidence of a growth-and-jobs rule framework. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`
- **President Tinubu: I have no cabal or sponsors to compensate** | State House | 2024-07-26 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-i-have-no-cabal-or-sponsors-to-compensate/) | Tinubu denied owing sponsors or a cabal, which is rhetorical but relevant as a counterpoint to claims that policy was being shaped purely to reward patrons. | `5B.4`, `5B.2`

**Negative / limiting evidence**

- **Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-07-31 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462) | Reuters reported inflation above 34 percent after subsidy removal, naira devaluation, and higher electricity tariffs, showing the rule changes had not yet created a stable or predictable environment for enterprise. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`
- **Hundreds gather across Nigerian cities to protest cost-of-living crisis** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-01 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376) | The protests were driven by cost-of-living pain and governance anger, which is strong evidence that the business and employment climate remained highly strained. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`
- **Insecurity, rising costs push 31 million Nigerians into acute food shortage, study says** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-27 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/insecurity-rising-costs-push-31-million-nigerians-into-acute-food-shortage-study-says-3589474) | Acute food insecurity on this scale is negative evidence for job creation and broad entrepreneurial conditions, because it signals that the economy was still failing large parts of the population. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`
- **FG spent N63.6bn on military equipment in seven months - Report** | Punch | 2024-08-17 | [URL](https://punchng.com/fg-spent-n63-6bn-on-military-equipment-in-seven-months-report/) | Weakly disclosed spending on military equipment raises transparency and diversion concerns, which is negative for fair public-finance rules and investment trust. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`
- **Nigeria’s Tinubu names seven ministers, sacks five in cabinet reshuffle** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-10-23 | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/nigerias-tinubu-names-seven-ministers-sacks-five-in-cabinet-reshuffle/2325625/) | The reshuffle looked ordinary rather than a loyalty purge, so it is only weak negative/neutral evidence; it does not show strong institutional rule-building in itself. | `5B.4`, `5B.2`
- **Nigeria considers tough penalties for subversive acts under proposed law** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-14 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/nigeria-considers-tough-penalties-for-subversive-acts-under-proposed-law-3571782) | A proposed Counter Subversion Bill criticized as a crackdown on dissent would have chilled protest and public contestation, which is bad for entrepreneurship and investment confidence. | `5B.4`, `5B.10`, `5B.4`
- **Nigeria protesters charged treason, inciting military** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-09-02 | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/nigeria-charges-protesters-with-treason-inciting-military/2249248/) | Treason/mutiny charges against protesters show a punitive legal climate, which can deter legitimate dissent and raise the political risk premium for investors and entrepreneurs. | `5B.4`, `5B.10`, `5B.4`
- **Nigeria police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/) | Excessive-force crackdowns and mass detentions signal a coercive operating environment, which is negative for job creation and fair competition because it chills public challenge and policy feedback. | `5B.4`, `5B.10`, `5B.4`

**Search gap**
I found strong evidence on macro reform, procurement, and technocratic institutions, but weaker direct evidence on competition policy, antitrust enforcement, property-rights adjudication, and trade-rule reform in 2024. The clearest negatives are indirect: coercive crisis politics, high inflation, and opacity around some spending, rather than a single obvious anti-competition law or property-rights violation.
